issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) (an int parameter), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) (a double parameter). This is a parameter type mismatch between the specification and the provided solution reference and will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Pneumatic.raisePressure signature consistent with the UML/problem statement. Change the interface declaration in Pneumatic.java to use an int parameter: void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease); and update any references/implementations accordingly. Alternatively, if double is intended, update the UML/problem statement to specify double and clarify the change.
